Latin word

nūntius

nūntius, nūntiī m.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

news, a message; a messenger; a message, news; messenger; news, a message, tidings (especially news brought by someone)

In this lexicon

  • information

    also used · classical · Catull. 9.5: ō mihi nūntiī beātī!

  • message

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 4.12.1: nōn jūcundissimum mē nūntium vōbīs allātūrum; Traupman 261, 345: nūntius, message

  • messenger

    the recommended word · classical

  • news

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Stich. 2.2.67: nūntium exoptābilem nūntiāre (Lewis & Short); Traupman 350

  • nūntius scrīptus: text message

    modern

  • nūntius vōcālis: voicemail

    modern

  • nūntius meteōrologicus: weather forecaster

    modern

Examples

  • etsī sciō nōn jūcundissimum mē nūntium vōbīs allātūrum, tamen … vīsum est faciendum, quōquō modō rēs sē habēret, vōs certiōrēs facere.

    Although I know that the message I bring you is far from welcome, … I thought I should let you know how things stand, whatever they are.Cic. Fam. 4.12.1
